items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Bill and I were invited down to the Greenwich Village home of Alfred and Lorraine Lion

ctx.x: No, I wanted to make sure what you were taking about.

Fine. Okay. The world has gone on to other forms of waylaying people. I mean I’m not old enough to have been around when the press gangs were kidnapping sailors and putting them on ships in the harbor, but this is almost it. But no the point is so what I’m saying is it’s a combination of a certain amount of osmosis. Pop music was in the air to a very large extent and it was very close to being or actually was jazz at this point, and then also physical circumstances made it possible for me to have direct listening…

in those days that I did not realize the impossibility of what I wisely set out to do, but on the spot it was a big, sprawling Greenwich Village studio living room, Monk and I went off into a corner disregarding all the other people there and I interviewed him for an article that appeared in the magazine.
